title: Micro run tally — Playlet (personal)
content:
Purpose: quick personal tally of small-batch inference runs while poking at prefix caching + aggressive batching heuristics. Lightweight table + hunches. Not official results, do not share as bench summary.

Table (CSV-ish):
run_id,date,model,batch_size,avg_seq,p50_ms,p95_ms,tokens_per_sec,cost_per_1k_notes,notes
R-001,2025-01-13,redwood-lite-7B,1,64,28,72,410,0.42,baseline single-request w/o prefix cache
R-002,2025-01-13,redwood-lite-7B,4,64,31,88,1250,0.27,naive batching (concat) increases p95 a bit
R-003,2025-01-14,redwood-lite-7B,4,64,23,60,1450,0.24,batching + prefix-cache (warm) drops p50 by ~25%
R-004,2025-01-14,redwood-lite-7B,8,32,19,46,2200,0.18,shorter seqs + larger batches = best throughput; CPU spikes on host
R-005,2025-01-15,redwood-quant-7B,4,64,26,70,980,0.15,8-bit quant kernel; p50 similar, cost down
R-006,2025-01-16,redwood-lite-7B,2,256,110,240,290,0.65,long context hurts tail and throughput; memory pressure
R-007,2025-01-18,redwood-lite-7B,4,64,21,52,1380,0.25,retry after small GC patch; p95 improved
R-008,2025-01-20,redwood-lite-7B,16,16,17,40,3400,0.14,stress test: queueing visible, latency still acceptable for batchy workloads

Quick obs:
- Warm prefix cache is a huge win for p50; p95 improves but depends on backend GC/eviction timing.
- Batch size tradeoff: above ~8 tokens/batch throughput wins but tail increases if host CPU saturates. Need kernel + host balance.
- Quantized (8-bit) kernel shows ~40% cost saving in my small runs with modest latency change — promising for Dedicated pricing tiers.
- Long contexts (256) blow up p95 and lower tokens/sec drastically; consider adaptive batching or fragmentation.

Hypotheses to test next:
- If we add staggered batch release (small initial batch to satisfy low-latency requests + flush larger batches every 5ms), p95 will drop without much hit to tokens/sec.
- Tighter GC tuning (reduce pause) will reduce p95 for batched workloads.
- Switching to quantized kernel + dynamic KV spilling will keep p50 low for long contexts but need to test accuracy drift.

Short TODO / next steps:
- [ ] Create a controlled run harness for R-002..R-004 duplicate runs (script: bench/playlet-mini.sh) — map out warm vs cold cache explicitly. (linked GH PR above)
- [ ] Add CPU/RAM host traces to the table for runs where p95 increased (focus R-002,R-006)
- [ ] Try staggered-batch patch: prototype in local runtime branch (INF-1927)
- [ ] Quick eval for quantized outputs on the small QA prompt set (10 prompts) to eyeball fidelity

Notes-to-self / messy:
- Remember: these are single-node dev cluster runs — numbers will not match prod Dedicated clusters. Use as directional signals only.
- Slack thread: #runtime-bench has the raw perf logs for R-003 and R-007 (search "playlet-warm-cache").
- If pruning KV cache aggressively, measure miss rate per minute (idea: tiny counter at cache layer).

Appendix: sample minimal command I used (local):
./run_bench --model redwood-lite-7B --batch 4 --seq 64 --warm-cache 1 --repeat 50 --measure tail,p50,tokens

End of sheet.
